face: So you are the one who spilled the blood of my kinsmen, {player}. Sit in the mud and count the hours you have left to regret it.
Your footprints are still fresh in this muck, and I will follow them to the last field you ever plough. Do not mistake my silence for mercy.
A pity. Had you come to my table as a guest, I might have poured you wine. Instead you will kneel in the dirt until my liege decides your fate.
Spare me your pleading, ser. One who breaks an oath to the crown has forfeited every kind word.
Every hour you draw breath under my watch is a debt your house will pay in full. I swear it upon my father's grave.
The ravens will feast well on the ground you chose. Look at them circling, {player}, and tell me again how clever your ambush was.
Tighten those bonds. I trust no hand that once raised a blade against {my_faction}, and yours is no exception.
Mock me as you wish now. The day will come when the bards sing of your fall on these stones, and I shall be there to hear every verse.
Stand still, ser, and keep your hands where I can see them. What you do next will decide how long this march takes.
I have no quarrel with you personally. War is a ledger, and today you are merely an entry in mine.
Ransom is the only language of the road I trust. Your kin may pay {gold} for your return, and then we shall see whether they value you enough.
Walk when I say walk. The sun is cruel on this road, and I would rather not carry you the whole way.
You fought well enough for a stranger to these fields. Remember that when the scribes ask whether you were honourable.
Do not expect courtesy from me, nor cruelty either. Both are expensive, and I have spent my allowance for today.
A captive's life is a tedious thing to keep. Let us hope your kinsmen answer swiftly, before my patience and the rations both run thin.
Thirty years I have marched under {my_faction}, and I have learned that prisoners are mostly good for talking. Talk, then, ser.
Well fought, ser {player}. Had the fortune turned a single hand, I would be the one shackled here, and I would bear it with grace.
You spared my squire when you had every reason not to. I will remember that at whatever table the oaths are sworn.
Forgive the chains, friend. They are the custom of the road, not the mark of my regard for you.
Sit by the fire while we wait for word, traveller. A worthy foe is a rare companion, and I find I enjoy your company.
Carry your name high, ser {player}. Should our paths cross again on better ground, I will raise a cup in your honour.
Your father would be proud of how you held that ridge, I am certain of it. Tell me, what do the bards in your land call you?
I bear you no grudge, ser. My ransom can wait. Let us speak of harvests and old songs until the envoy arrives.
If the scribes ask how I was taken, I shall tell them I was bested by a worthy opponent. Few will argue with that account.
